summary: Lemons get a 20% chance to carry Token: each scored Token Lemon pays you half your current Interest in coins.
tip: A 1-ticket interest earner: Lemons tie Cherries as the most common symbol, so Tokens show up often. Raise Interest with Stonks or Grandma's Purse; add Lemon chance or fruit retriggers.

synergies.why: +5% Interest: at base Interest each Token pays about 70% more.
Doubles your Interest, so every Token pays double.
+15% Interest at first (fading 3% per Round) roughly triples what each Token pays.
+1 Lemon chance for good means more Token Lemons scored.
+2 Lemon chance for the Deadline means more Token Lemons scored.
Retriggered Lemon Patterns pay their Tokens again.

antiSynergies.why: Halves the base chance of Lemons, so fewer Tokens.
You can only deposit after the last Round, so Interest, and every Token payout, stays low during the Deadline.

assumptions: A Token pays half of the Interest payout (your Interest % of the deposit), the same amount basis Lucky Cat pays in full.
Retriggered Patterns pay their Tokens again (the wiki's strategy notes for these charms say so).

summary: Every spin with 3+ Patterns permanently raises Lemons and Cherries by their base value (+2 each).
tip: Scales fruit for good: Luck and retriggers make 3+ Pattern spins far more common, and the raised values stay if you sell it. All four Aces fuse into Poker Deck (DLC).

synergies.why: Fruit Patterns trigger twice, so two fruit Patterns already count as 4.
Repetition retriggers push spins to 3+ Patterns.
On 35% of spins every Pattern triggers again, so 2 Patterns count as 4.
Luck+7 on each Round's last spin gives about a 40% shot at 3+ Patterns.
Doubles the fruit value it has built up; take it later.
With Ace of Diamonds, Spades and Clubs, fuses into Poker Deck (DLC).

antiSynergies.why: Halves Lemon and Cherry chances, so the raised fruit is scored less often.

assumptions: Retriggers count toward the 3+ Patterns, as for Lucky Cat.
The raise is permanent symbol value, so it stays after the charm is sold.

summary: Every 3 tickets you spend in the store permanently raise Clovers and Bells by their base value (+3 each).
tip: It does nothing while spinning, so if you have a drawer, park it there and equip it only to shop. Ticket income (Thimble, Iron, Raging Capitalist) means more raises. Aces fuse into Poker Deck (DLC).

effects.note: Counts tickets spent at the store, not purchases: every 3 tickets spent raise Clovers and Bells by +3. One raise per purchase approximates a 2-4 ticket charm; free charms and phone rerolls add nothing.

synergies.why: Ticket Clovers fund more shopping, and Clovers are one of the symbols it raises.
Ticket Bells fund more shopping, and Bells are one of the symbols it raises.
Its Ticket modifiers fund more purchases, and every purchase grows it too.
Its 2-ticket price counts toward the next raise, and it refunds 4.
Doubles the Clover and Bell values it has built up; take it later.

antiSynergies.why: Halves Clover and Bell chances, so the raised symbols show up less.

assumptions: Spent tickets are counted cumulatively, so leftovers carry over to the next purchase.
Modelled as one raise per purchase (when.on purchase), matching an average charm price of about 3 tickets.
The ticket price of Ace of Clubs itself does not count.

synergies.why: Forces Above/Below after 3 spins without a 5+ Pattern: a guaranteed trigger.

More Diamonds on the grid to cash in the raised value.
More Treasures on the grid to cash in the raised value.

assumptions: Fires once per spin however many 4+ Patterns score, and a 4+ Pattern of any symbol counts.

Halves the Seven's chance, so the raised Seven shows up less.

assumptions: Read as 7 activations of any equipped charms (not 7 different charms), with the count carrying over between Rounds.
Always-on passive charms (Stonks, Cat Food) are assumed not to count as triggering.

summary: Randomly rolled: 1 downside plus 2 upsides, from huge (every Pattern retriggers, Symbols Mult +5, Patterns Mult +3) to small (+3 tickets).
tip: Read the roll before buying: 'all Patterns trigger again', SM +5, PM +3 and +2 spins are great; -3 spins and +3% 666 hurt most. A drawer keeps a good roll; Vorago re-rolls a bad one.

effects.text: Each copy rolls 1 downside when it spawns and keeps it: 666 chance +1.5%; 666 chance +3%; -2 spins per Round; -3 spins per Round (minimum 1 spin); discard after 3 Rounds; or discard after 5 Rounds.

Each copy also rolls 2 different upsides: all Patterns trigger one more time; +5% Interest; Symbols Multiplier +5; Patterns Multiplier +3; +3 Tickets at the end of every Deadline; Luck+5 on the first spin of every Round; +2 spins per Round; Lemons+Cherries, Clovers+Bells, Diamonds+Treasures or Sevens manifest more often (+2); or +2 Free Restocks when a Deadline begins.

synergies.why: Discard a bad Jimbo, then Vorago, to respawn it with a fresh roll.
Jimbo and D20 fuse into Booster Pack (DLC).
+2 spins per Round cancels a -2 spins downside.
Blocks the next 666 if the downside raised your 666 chance.
Each 666 from a 666-chance downside also hands out extra spins (+3, +2, +1 per Round).

assumptions: The effects are rolled per copy and cannot be simulated, so the ratings describe an average roll.
Assumed every listed option is equally likely; the +2 symbol-chance upside comes in four versions.
provides lists what a roll can give, not what every copy has.
Drawer storage and the Vorago re-roll come from the wiki's strategy notes.

summary: 30% chance each spin to reroll every symbol that is not part of a Pattern, giving the spin a second shot at more Patterns.
tip: Cheap, steady extra Patterns at any stage. Horseshoe makes it 60%, and its frequent activations feed Tarot Deck, Channeler of Fortune and Ace of Spades.

synergies.why: Doubles its chance to 60%.
Guarantees the reroll on the spin you choose.
Fires on about 30% of spins, helping keep the streak going.
A cheap, frequent activation toward its 5 per Round.
Each activation counts toward its 7, growing the Seven.

assumptions: Assumed the reroll happens before scoring, so Patterns it forms score in the same spin; symbols already in a Pattern stay put.

summary: At the end of every Round the store restocks for free, so you see a fresh set of charms each Round without paying coins.
tip: Good for hunting key charms. Unbought offers vanish at Round end, so buy what you want first. Refills First Love's empty store and lets Shopping Cart keep its hoard.

effects.text: The free restock happens automatically when each Round ends and cannot be saved: it does not add to the free restocks you hold, and any offers you did not buy are replaced.

synergies.why: Refreshes the store every Round without spending the free restocks the Cart counts.
That memory card starts each Deadline with an empty store; D6 refills it after every Round.
7 one-spin Rounds per Deadline means 7 free restocks.
A fresh store each Round supplies cheap charms to buy and sell as fodder.

antiSynergies.why: Only 1 Round per Deadline, so it restocks just once.

assumptions: Valued as one free restock per Round.
The wiki says item-forced restocks (Fortune Cookie, Cigarettes) do not count as restocks, so D6 probably does not feed Bell Pepper or Electricity Meter; they are not listed as synergies.

summary: At the end of every Round, each charm in your drawers is swapped for a new random charm.
tip: Needs unlocked drawers. Park cheap charms there and collect a fresh random charm per drawer each Round: keep the good ones or sell them (great with Dung Beetle). Never store charms you need.

effects.text: At each Round's end every charm stored in a drawer is replaced by a random new one and the old charm is lost; empty drawers stay empty, so leave a charm in each drawer to keep rolling. Charms on the table are not affected.

synergies.why: Sell the new drawer charms (refill the drawer with a cheap one): each sale grows the Beetle and pays tickets.
D20 and Jimbo fuse into Booster Pack (DLC).

antiSynergies.why: Usually parked in a drawer until a phone call, where D20 would replace it.
Kept in a drawer as death insurance, where D20 would replace it.
Its drawer trick fails: D20 replaces it while it waits there.

assumptions: Assumed the new charms come from the normal store pool and sell for their usual resell value.
Assumed the replaced charms do not count as discards (no Dung Beetle stack or Vorago ban for them).
Assumed D20 must be on the table, not in a drawer, to work.

summary: Red Button (6 charges): adds a random 2-symbol Pattern (HOR-S, VER-S or DIAG-S, worth x0.5) for the rest of the Round.
tip: Pairs line up constantly, so each press adds many small hits and big Pattern counts (Pentacle, Mushrooms, Lucky Cat). 6 charges is slow without charge help. While active, Halo rarely fires.

synergies.why: Half the presses cost no charge, so its 6-charge cost bites less.
Each press triggers twice, often adding two different small Patterns.
Small Patterns push spins past 5 Patterns, growing its Symbols Multiplier.
Every Pattern past the second raises all Symbols for the Round.
Small Patterns make 3+ Pattern spins routine, so it pays Interest often.
Doubles small Patterns, the 2-symbol ones included.

antiSynergies.why: Pairs form so easily that spins rarely have exactly one Pattern.
Needs a lone Pattern, which small Patterns make rare.
Needs a lone Diamond or Treasure Pattern, which small Patterns make rare.

assumptions: A 2-symbol Pattern only scores where no bigger Pattern covers it.
Per the wiki, up to 3 presses can unlock all three small Patterns; extra presses add nothing.

summary: Each time you score an Eye Pattern, you earn again the total coins that all your 999s have paid so far this run.
tip: A Sacred Mode payoff that grows with every 999. Eye Jar forces Eyes, and a full-grid Jackpot includes an Eye, so Luck builds and Ophanim Wheels cash it in often. Useless before a 999.

effects.text: Whenever an Eye Pattern scores (alone or with others, including the Eye inside a full-grid Jackpot), you earn again the total coins earned from every 999 so far this run. Pays nothing before your first 999.

synergies.why: Forces the Eye after 3 gem spins in a row, cashing the 999 total again.
Each 999 forces a Jackpot next spin, and its Eye pays the fresh total at once.
Spreading a lone Pattern can fill an Eye or the whole grid (a Jackpot), and each Eye repays your 999 total.
Its guaranteed Jackpot includes an Eye.
In Sacred Mode its +3% 666 chance means more 999s to bank.
Its forced 666 lands as a 999 in Sacred Mode (from Deadline 3), growing the total each Eye repays.

antiSynergies.why: Assumed to cancel 999s like 666s, so fewer 999s to bank.

assumptions: A 999 pays the coins earned so far in that Round; Eye of God repays the run total of those bonuses each time.
Assumed a full-grid Jackpot counts as scoring an Eye, since Jackpots do not hide smaller Patterns.
Assumed 666-chance charms raise 999 chance in Sacred Mode (all 6s become 9s) and that Holy Bible cancels 999s because they count as 666s for charms.

summary: Every 999 gives each charm on your table a random Trait, replacing any Trait it already had.
tip: Your first 999 gives every charm on the table a Trait and later ones re-roll them, so it is huge with The Collector. Necronomicon and Book of Shadows raise your 999 odds.

effects.text: A charm holds only one Trait, so each 999 re-rolls the Trait of every charm on the table, good ones included; charms in drawers or bought later get nothing until the next 999.

synergies.why: Every traited charm adds Patterns Multiplier +1, so one 999 can add about +7.
Turns the Avid and Ambitious Traits it hands out into x2 multipliers (DLC).
In Sacred Mode its +3% 666 chance becomes +3% 999 chance.
+1.5% 999 chance in Sacred Mode, plus extra spins after each one.
Its forced 666 lands as a 999 in Sacred Mode (from Deadline 3), so new charms get Traits on demand.

antiSynergies.why: Assumed to cancel 999s like 666s, wasting the trigger.

assumptions: Read 'a random Trait' as each charm rolling its own Trait; it may be one shared Trait for all.
Devious adds 666 chance, which becomes 999 chance in Sacred Mode, so it is not a drawback here.
Assumed 666-chance charms raise 999 chance in Sacred Mode and that Holy Bible cancels 999s because they count as 666s for charms.

summary: Each Red Button press has a 50% chance to use no charges, so button charms fire about twice as often.
tip: Roughly doubles uses of Midas Touch, Number 1/2, Ring Bell and the Pictures, without Nuclear Button's -1 slot. Useless without button charms. Fuses into Glorious Trumpet (DLC).

synergies.why: More presses means more Rounds of permanent symbol growth.
Every free press is another permanent +1 Symbols Multiplier.
Free presses make Rounds of yellow retriggers far more frequent.
Saving its 12-charge cost half the time means extra Rounds much more often.
Free presses still trigger twice; with Horseshoe the three fuse into Glorious Trumpet (DLC).
With Nuclear Button, the three fuse into Glorious Trumpet (DLC).

assumptions: Assumed the 50% roll is made per press and a free press still triggers every charged charm.

summary: When a spin has exactly one Pattern, every symbol touching it turns into that Pattern's symbol, usually forming much bigger Patterns.
tip: Lone Patterns come up on about 3 spins in 10, and each spread builds big Patterns, often doubling or tripling your coins. Little Star, Stain and Vine's Soup love it; Angel's Hand hurts it.

synergies.why: Its forced middle-row HOR-XL, when alone, spreads over the whole grid: a Jackpot.
The spread usually makes a 4+ Pattern, raising all Patterns for the Round.
Each spread that makes a 4+ Pattern raises Diamonds and Treasures for good.
Doubles the big Patterns the spread creates.
A spread often scores 5+ Patterns at once, doubling Symbols for the Round.
A spread often scores 5+ Patterns at once, growing its Symbols Multiplier.

antiSynergies.why: Its 2-symbol Patterns form so easily that spins rarely have exactly one Pattern.

assumptions: Assumed 'adjacent' includes diagonal neighbours, as the simulator does; with side neighbours only, a centred middle-row HOR still grows into an Eye and a lone middle-row HOR-XL still fills the grid.
Assumed the transformed grid scores in the same spin.
Tier S from simulation: in a plain build it multiplied coins about 2.4-3x with side-only adjacency and 3.5-4.6x with diagonals.

summary: Lemons and Cherries get 15% Repetition, Clovers and Bells 5% Battery, and Diamonds, Treasures and Sevens 15% Chain.
tip: Three modifier charms in one slot: fruit Repetition retriggers the commonest Patterns, gem Chains permanently raise the Patterns they score in, and Battery fuels Red Button builds.

synergies.why: Repetition chances add up to 30% on Lemons and Cherries.
Fruit Patterns trigger again on top of their Repetition retriggers.
Chain chances add up to 27% on Diamonds, Treasures and Sevens.
Battery chances add up to 11% on Clovers and Bells.
Its Token fruit gets re-scored by The Blood's Repetition retriggers.
Repetition retriggers score Golden Lemons again, so Lemon value grows faster.

assumptions: The Chain line has no '+' sign but is read as +15% like the others.
